description: Review code changes for bugs, security issues, and style before they ship.
instructions: When reviewing code: 1) Read the changed files fully with read_file. 2) Check for logic bugs, off-by-one errors, unhandled edge cases, and broken error handling. 3) Flag security issues: injection, leaked secrets, unsafe deserialization, missing auth checks. 4) Note style or maintainability problems briefly. 5) End with a clear verdict: approve, or list blocking issues first, then nits. Be specific with file paths and line numbers. Do not rewrite the code unless asked.
name: Code Review

description: Add meaningful tests that catch real bugs in the selected code.
instructions: When asked to write tests: 1) Read the code under test first. 2) Prefer tests that catch real bugs: edge cases, error paths, and regressions over trivial happy-path assertions. 3) Match the repo's existing test framework and style; check how current tests are written before adding new ones. 4) Keep each test focused on one behavior with a clear name. 5) Run the new tests with the project's runner and fix failures before finishing. Ask before changing production code to make tests pass.
name: Write Tests

description: Explain what code does in plain language, from the big picture down.
instructions: When explaining code: 1) Start with one sentence on what the code is for. 2) Then describe the main flow step by step, naming the key functions and files. 3) Explain any tricky or non-obvious parts. 4) Keep it plain and skimmable; use short paragraphs, not walls of text. 5) Make no changes to the code.
name: Explain Code

description: Reproduce a bug, fix it, and verify the fix with a test.
instructions: When fixing a bug: 1) Reproduce it first — write a minimal reproduction or failing test before changing anything. 2) Find the root cause, not just the symptom; explain it in one or two sentences. 3) Make the smallest fix that addresses the cause. 4) Re-run the reproduction to confirm it is fixed, and run the surrounding test suite for regressions. 5) Summarize what broke, what changed, and how it was verified.
name: Fix Bug

description: Ship finished changes as a GitHub pull request.
instructions: When asked to open a pull request: 1) Review the changes with the diff or read_file to make sure they are complete and tests pass. 2) Use github_create_pr with a clear title, a short body describing what changed and why, and the full set of changed files. 3) Target the repo's default branch unless told otherwise. 4) Report the PR URL when done. Never push directly to the default branch.
name: Open PR
